hero.title: NutriLogic Expert System
hero.subtitle: A rule-based nutrition intelligence engine tailored to East African dietary contexts and consumer decision support.

origin.pullQuote: Health guidance becomes useful only when it reflects local food realities.
paragraphs: NutriLogic was initiated to bridge a localization gap in consumer nutrition tools: many systems provide generic advice that ignores culturally specific ingredients, meal patterns, and affordability constraints.
The project uses an expert-system approach to encode transparent dietary logic that can be reviewed, refined, and adapted as new regional nutrition knowledge is introduced.

architecture.title: Rule-Driven Dietary Inference Layer
architecture.description: A knowledge-base architecture that evaluates food profiles against condition-aware nutrition rules.
architecture.narrative: The system separates knowledge representation from inference execution. Nutritional rules are encoded in explicit condition-action structures, making outcomes explainable and easier to audit. Input normalization layers convert user-provided meal context into standard attributes before rule evaluation, enabling consistent recommendations.

hardParts.title: Resolving Conflicting Nutrition Rules Across Conditions
hardParts.description: The core challenge was handling contradictory recommendations for users with multiple dietary constraints.
hardParts.narrative: Single-condition logic worked well, but multi-condition profiles produced recommendation conflicts. The fix introduced a precedence and conflict-resolution layer that merges condition-specific outputs into a consistent final verdict, while preserving traceability of why that verdict was chosen.
